```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,message=FALSE)
library(capnet); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(lubridate)
repo_root <- normalizePath("../..")
source("helpers.R"); source("experiments.R")
results_dir <- file.path(repo_root,"manuscript/results")
results <- if(params$rerun) paper_finance() else readRDS(file.path(results_dir,"finance.rds"))
```

## Protocol

The bundled `inst/extdata/data.csv` contains daily market observations through
2026-02-13. We use the eleven feature columns listed below, without constructing
additional predictors. Training windows are 25 calendar years, refit monthly;
the evaluation starts in January 2020. Complete training cases are used. The
historical training window stays fixed as the cap penalty walks over individual
rows in the following month (`walk = 1`).

```{r data}
data <- paper_finance_data()
names(data)
calc_moments(data[,results$feature_cols])
```

At each refit, `cv.glmnet` selects `lambda.min` with `alpha = 0.5`, ten random
folds, and standardization. Monthly seeds start at 42 and increase by one.
This lambda is shared across methods and gamma values. Random inner folds
are retained from the original vignette; the outer evaluation remains
chronological. This design is not forward-chaining inner validation.

Ceilings use the original helper rule
$L_j=7|\mathrm{cor}(X_j,y)|/350$ on the complete training cases. This is a
scale-dependent correlation heuristic, not a univariate slope rule.
The ordinary `capnet` fit with `gamma = 0` supplies the uncapped model;
post-fit capping clips its contributions and retains its intercept. The
walk-forward grid is `c(0.1, 1, 10, 100)`.

The data are taken as supplied by the competition. Their proprietary feature
release times cannot be independently verified from this file; no portfolio
return or investment-risk guarantee is inferred from these forecast results.

```{r compute-definition}
# Exact shared definition used by tools/run_paper_experiments.R:
paper_finance
```

## Forecast scores

`calc_oos_r2` reports one pooled squared-error score,
$1-\sum(y_t-\hat y_t)^2/\sum(y_t-\bar y_{t-1})^2$.
The benchmark averages preceding **evaluation-period** responses, not initial
training responses, and omits the first evaluation observation. This is not
an average of monthly R-squared values.

```{r scores}
knitr::kable(paper_scores(results,"X"),digits=6)
```

## Rolling performance and corrected contribution diagnostic

The illustrative walk-forward specification uses gamma 0.1, fixed in this
report rather than selected from the plotted evaluation window. Rolling
scores use 252 scored observations. Each contribution series is computed as
`apply(abs(contribution_matrix), 1, max)` **separately for each model**.
Feature columns are selected by name; metadata never enters the maximum.

```{r plots,fig.width=9,fig.height=5.6}
plots <- paper_plots(results,"X",gamma=.1,window=252)
plots$rolling
plots$contributions
```

```{r snapshot}
knitr::kable(paper_snapshot(results,"X","2023-05-24",.1,results$feature_cols,1e4),digits=3)
```

The snapshot scales contributions by $10^4$; the intercept is excluded.

## Numerical diagnostics

```{r diagnostics}
stopifnot(all(is.finite(as.numeric(results$predictions$predicted))))
results$diagnostics |> group_by(method,requested_gamma) |>
  summarise(missing=sum(missing),
    reduced_rows=sum(effective_gamma<requested_gamma,na.rm=TRUE),
    unsuccessful_stops=sum(!is.na(convergence)&convergence<0&convergence != -1001),
    .groups="drop")
```

## Runtime protocol

Runtime uses three serial repetitions of the entire backtest for each of
`glmnet`, `capnet`, and `walk_capnet`, including monthly CV and output assembly.
The two contribution-penalized methods both use **gamma 0.1**. The same monthly
seeds and lambda-search defaults are used in every repetition. The initial
package installation/loading is excluded. Requested BLAS/OpenMP thread limits
are one, and no experiment-level parallelism is used for these timings.
Reported numbers describe this machine and run, not portable solver rankings.

```{r runtime}
knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path(results_dir,"runtime-summary.csv")),digits=2)
```

Run `bash tools/reproduce_paper.sh` from the repository root for a fresh
source install and all computations. Render this report with
`params = list(rerun = TRUE)` to rerun its fitting step independently. Full
predictions, convergence diagnostics, package versions, and input/source MD5
checksums are saved in `manuscript/results/finance*` and `runtime*`.
